# ModGuard · `v1.0.0-beta1` ![status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-beta-orange) ![version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.0.0--beta1-blue) ![platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android-8.0%2B%20(API%2026)-green) ![root](https://img.shields.io/badge/root-APatch%20tested%20%C2%B7%20Magisk%2FKSU%20untested-purple) ![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-lightgrey) > **A security scanner for root modules** — like "Play Protect" for APatch / Magisk / KernelSU modules. ModGuard statically scans a root module (`.zip` before install, or an already‑installed module under `/data/adb/modules/`), assigns a risk **verdict** — **CLEAN / WARNING / DANGER** — and can keep watching installed modules for tampering. Everything runs **on‑device**; nothing is uploaded unless you explicitly enable VirusTotal. > ⚠️ **Beta / compatibility notice.** This is an early beta. It has been **tested on APatch only**. > The design targets Magisk and KernelSU too (module layout, BusyBox paths, and env detection are > handled), but those have **not been verified on real devices yet**. Treat verdicts as an *extra > layer of defense*, not a guarantee. --- ## Table of contents - [Features](#features) - [How it works](#how-it-works) - [Screens](#screens) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Install](#install) - [Build from source](#build-from-source) - [Project structure](#project-structure) - [Detection rules](#detection-rules) - [Security & privacy notes](#security--privacy-notes) - [Support](#support) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [License](#license) - [Disclaimer](#disclaimer) --- ## Features - **Device security score** — the Home tab shows an overall root‑security score (0–100) plus a breakdown of dangerous / warning / ignored modules. - **Pre‑install scan** — pick a module `.zip`, get a verdict and a detailed, explainable list of findings (file, line, snippet, plain‑language reason) before you flash it. - **Install gate** — CLEAN installs freely; WARNING asks for confirmation; DANGER is blocked unless you override with **fingerprint / device PIN** (biometric prompt). - **Installed‑module scanning** — list modules in `/data/adb/modules/` and scan any of them on demand (root). - **Static payload de‑obfuscation** — hidden `base64` / `base64+gzip` / hex payloads are **decoded as data (never executed)** and re‑scanned, so a concealed `wget … | sh` is revealed. The decoded plaintext is shown to you; an undecodable (encrypted) payload is flagged instead of hidden. - **Database‑driven verdicts** — "there's base64" is treated as a *weak* signal to avoid false positives; a **DANGER** verdict is driven by the offline hash database, VirusTotal, or the actual decoded content. - **VirusTotal (optional, hash‑first)** — sends the SHA‑256 first; results are **cached for offline** use. Public‑API rate limits (4/min, 500/day) are enforced automatically. Set the key in‑app; it's synced to the module via root. - **Offline antivirus database** — a local hash blocklist + regex signatures, extendable from any source (see [`apatch-module/DATABASE.md`](apatch-module/DATABASE.md)). - **Realtime guard (root module)** — a lightweight `inotifyd` service (sleeps in the kernel, near‑zero idle cost) that scans a module the moment it is **installed or updated** — no reboot, no full sweep of existing modules. Updating the ModGuard module itself re‑activates without a reboot too. - **Baseline & diff monitoring** — event‑driven (app open + boot + WorkManager), no polling daemon. Volatile manager / magic‑mount files are excluded and non‑security changes don't alert, to avoid false positives on magic‑mount setups. - **Ignore list** — mark a module as safe so it stops notifying; keyed by **id + version**, so file churn (e.g. magic mount) won't un‑ignore it, but a real update re‑arms the warning. - **Status / diagnostics tab** — permissions & access, all ModGuard services, and an on‑device crash log. - **English & Indonesian** — the UI follows your system language. - **CLI + recovery** — the same `:core` engine as a Termux‑runnable JAR, plus a pure‑shell scanner for OrangeFox recovery. --- ## How it works ### Pre‑install scan & gate ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Pick module .zip] --> B[ZipModuleReader: parse module.prop,
extract scripts, hash files] B --> C[Rule engine :core
regex + heuristics] C --> D[PayloadDecoder
decode base64/gzip/hex as DATA] D --> E[Re-scan decoded content] E --> F[ScoreCalculator: sum weights, clamp 0-100] F --> G{Verdict} G -->|CLEAN <30| H[Install allowed] G -->|WARNING 30-69| I[Confirm dialog] G -->|DANGER >=70| J[Blocked] J --> K[Override needs
fingerprint / PIN] C -.optional.-> V[VirusTotal hash-first
+ offline cache] V --> F I -->|proceed| H K -->|verified| H H --> L[Call APatch installer via su] ``` ### Realtime guard (root module) ```mermaid flowchart LR S[install/update event] --> W[inotifyd watches modules
+ modules_update staging] W -->|module installed/updated| X[debounce, compute fingerprint] X --> Y{in per-fingerprint cache?} Y -->|unchanged| Z[skip - no re-scan, no alert] Y -->|new / updated| Q[scan: static + offline DB + VirusTotal] Q --> R{DANGER and not ignored?} R -->|yes| N[log + am broadcast -> app notification] R -->|no| Z ``` Purely event‑driven: it scans a module only when it is **installed or updated** (the staging dir is watched, so this needs **no reboot**), never sweeps already‑installed modules, and skips its own module. The app and module compute an **identical canonical fingerprint** (`SHA‑256` over sorted `relpath:filehash`, excluding volatile manager / magic‑mount files), so caching and the ignore list work across both. --- ## Screens > 📸 Screenshots are not bundled yet (beta). Contributions welcome — drop PNGs in `docs/screenshots/` > and link them here. Navigation is a **bottom bar** with five tabs, plus two pushed screens: | Tab / screen | What it shows | |--------------|---------------| | **Home** | Device root‑security score (0–100) + dangerous / warning / ignored counts + guard status | | **Scan** | Pick a module `.zip` to scan before installing | | **Installed** | Modules under `/data/adb/modules/`, scan any on demand | | **Warnings** | Risky (not ignored) vs. ignored modules, with ignore / restore | | **Status** | Permissions & access, all ModGuard services, on‑device crash log | | *Scan result* (pushed) | Big verdict + score, module info, VirusTotal card, expandable findings (decoded payloads shown inline), install gate, "ignore" | | *Settings* (pushed) | Module service status, thresholds, offline AV database, monitoring, VirusTotal key, per‑rule toggles | --- ## Requirements | | | |---|---| | **Device** | Android 8.0+ (API 26) with root via **APatch** (tested), or Magisk / KernelSU (untested) | | **App** | The signed beta APK (see [Install](#install)) | | **Realtime module** | BusyBox with `inotifyd` (bundled by APatch/Magisk/KSU) + toybox `sha256sum` | | **VirusTotal (optional)** | A free VirusTotal API key | | **CLI (optional)** | A JVM — on Termux: `pkg install openjdk-17` | | **Build** | JDK 17, Android SDK (compileSdk 35), the bundled Gradle wrapper | --- ## Install ### App ```bash adb install dist/ModGuard-1.0.0-beta1.apk ``` If you previously installed a **debug** build, uninstall it first (different signature). Beta‑to‑beta updates install over each other without uninstalling. ### Realtime guard module (optional) Flash `dist/modguard-apatch.zip` in **APatch Manager → Modules → Install from storage**. Reboot once to activate the watcher (or open the app's **Status** tab and tap *Restart* to activate without a reboot). After that, module installs/updates are scanned live, and updating ModGuard itself needs no reboot. Set the VirusTotal key from the app (Settings → VirusTotal → Save) — the app writes it to `/data/adb/modguard/vt_api_key` via root automatically. ### CLI (optional, Termux) ```bash pkg install openjdk-17 java -jar modguard-cli.jar [--db ] [--json] # exit code: 0=CLEAN 1=WARNING 2=DANGER 3=error ``` ### Recovery (OrangeFox) ```sh sh scripts/modguard-recovery.sh ``` --- ## Build from source ```bash # Core unit tests (no device needed) ./gradlew :core:test # Debug APK ./gradlew :app:assembleDebug # app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk # Signed beta release APK (needs keystore.properties, see below) ./gradlew :app:assembleRelease # app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk # Full verification (compiles debug+release, lint, tests) ./gradlew build # CLI fat JAR ./gradlew :cli:fatJar # cli/build/libs/modguard-cli.jar # APatch module zip sh scripts/build-apatch-module.sh # dist/modguard-apatch.zip ``` ### Signing (for release builds) Release signing reads a **git‑ignored** `keystore.properties` at the repo root: ```properties storeFile=modguard-beta.keystore storePassword=your-store-password keyAlias=modguard keyPassword=your-key-password ``` Generate a keystore once (kept out of version control; reuse it so updates stay installable): ```bash keytool -genkeypair -v -keystore modguard-beta.keystore -alias modguard \ -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 ``` Without `keystore.properties`, the release build is produced **unsigned**. `minifyEnabled` is **off** in beta on purpose (avoids R8 breaking reflection in kotlinx‑serialization / Compose). --- ## Project structure ``` ModGuard/ ├── app/ # Android app (Kotlin + Jetpack Compose) │ └── src/main/kotlin/dev/tomoeisozaki/modguard/ │ ├── MainActivity.kt · ModGuardApplication.kt │ ├── auth/ # BiometricAuthenticator (DANGER override) │ ├── data/ # Settings, secure key, AV DB, VT cache, ignore list stores │ ├── diag/ # CrashLogger (uncaught-exception log for the Status tab) │ ├── monitor/ # Baseline/diff, WorkManager, notifications, boot/alert receivers │ ├── root/ # RootShell, installer, installed-module reader, ModuleBridge │ ├── scan/ # ScannerFactory (wires settings + AV DB into the engine) │ ├── vt/ # VtRepository (cache + rate limit) │ └── ui/ # MainScaffold (bottom nav) + home, scan, installed, threats, │ # status, result, settings, theme, components ├── core/ # Pure-JVM engine (no Android deps) — shared with CLI & module logic │ └── src/main/kotlin/dev/tomoeisozaki/modguard/core/ │ ├── model/ # ScanResult, Finding, Verdict, ModuleInfo, Signature, VtStats, … │ ├── scanner/ # ZipModuleReader, ModulePropParser, PayloadDecoder, ModuleScanner │ ├── rules/ # Rule engine, built-in rules, signature rules, scoring │ └── vt/ # VirusTotalClient (hash-first), RateLimiter ├── cli/ # Kotlin JVM CLI (fat JAR) — same :core engine ├── apatch-module/ # Root module: module.prop, service.sh, boot-completed.sh, │ # customize.sh, scan.sh (engine), DATABASE.md ├── scripts/ # build-apatch-module.sh, modguard-recovery.sh, modguard-scan ├── samples/ # Test module zips (clean / malicious / malformed) ├── dist/ # Release artifacts (APK, module zip, CLI jar) ├── gradle/libs.versions.toml # Version catalog └── MODGUARD_PLANNING.md # Original design brief ``` **Modules:** `:app` (UI + root/Android glue) depends on `:core`; `:cli` depends on `:core`; `:core` is pure JVM and Android‑free so the exact same detection logic runs in the app, the CLI, and (re‑implemented in shell) the recovery script. The APatch module's `scan.sh` mirrors a subset of the rules in POSIX shell for on‑device root scanning without a JVM. --- ## Detection rules Rule‑based (no ML). Each finding carries a weight; the sum (clamped 0–100) maps to the verdict (`<30` CLEAN, `30–69` WARNING, `>=70` DANGER; thresholds are configurable). DANGER is driven mainly by the **hash database / VirusTotal / decoded content**, not by weak heuristics like "base64 present." | Rule | Detects | Weight | |------|---------|--------| | `KNOWN_MALWARE_HASH` | file/module hash in offline AV database | +80 | | `VT_REPUTATION` | VirusTotal detections (dynamic) / clean bonus | +30…+90 / −30 | | `EXTERNAL_APK_INSTALL` | `pm install` / download‑and‑install APK | +45 | | `NET_FETCH_ON_BOOT` | `curl`/`wget` in boot scripts | +40 | | `*_DECODED` | dangerous content found **after** decoding a hidden payload | rule's weight | | `ENCRYPTED_PAYLOAD` | hidden payload that can't be decoded to text (encrypted/binary) | +40 | | `SENSITIVE_PATH_ACCESS` | `/data/data`, keystore, other root tools' dirs | +30 | | `NEW_SYSTEM_BINARY` | new binary in `system/bin|xbin|lib*` | +25 | | `CRON_PERSISTENCE` | cron / init.d persistence | +25 | | `SUSPICIOUS_SHELL` | `chmod 777`, `dd`, remount rw `/system` | +20 | | `OBFUSCATED_PAYLOAD` | `base64 -d` / `eval` present (weak signal) | +15 | | `PROP_INCOMPLETE` | missing `module.prop` fields | +10 | | signatures | regex from the offline AV database | configurable | --- ## Security & privacy notes - **On‑device by default.** Static analysis is local. VirusTotal is opt‑in and hash‑first; the actual module is only uploaded if you choose to. - **Payloads are never executed.** De‑obfuscation only *decodes* data (base64/gzip/hex). There is no sandbox execution — decoding data is strictly safer. - **Secrets** (VirusTotal key) are stored with `EncryptedSharedPreferences`, never hard‑coded. - **VirusTotal Public API is free but not for commercial products.** Fine for personal / free community use; commercial use requires a paid VirusTotal plan. - **Root responsibility.** The app requests `su` only to read `/data/adb/modules/` and to invoke the existing APatch installer — it does not reimplement flashing. --- ## Support If ModGuard is useful to you, you can support its development — thank you! ☕ [![Support me on Ko-fi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Support%20me%20on-Ko--fi-FF5E5B?logo=ko-fi&logoColor=white)](https://ko-fi.com/tomoeisozaki) [![Support on Saweria](https://img.shields.io/badge/Support%20on-Saweria-FAAA3C?logoColor=white)](https://saweria.co/tomoeisozaki) - **Ko-fi:** https://ko-fi.com/tomoeisozaki - **Saweria:** https://saweria.co/tomoeisozaki --- ## Contributing Bug reports, **Magisk / KernelSU compatibility results**, and new detection rules are welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for build/test steps, how to add a rule, and the invariants you must not break (canonical fingerprint; never execute scanned payloads; keep `:core` Android‑free). --- ## License Released under the [MIT License](LICENSE) © 2026 tomoeisozaki. Note: the optional VirusTotal Public API is free for **personal / non‑commercial** use only. --- ## Disclaimer ModGuard is a **defense‑in‑depth** aid, not a guarantee. Rule‑based static analysis can produce false positives and can miss sophisticated or encrypted payloads. Always use judgment before flashing modules with root privileges. This beta is provided **as‑is**, with no warranty.

ModGuard · `v1.0.0-beta1`

!status

!version

!platform-green)

!root

!license

> A security scanner for root modules — like "Play Protect" for APatch / Magisk / KernelSU modules.

ModGuard statically scans a root module (.zip before install, or an already‑installed

module under /data/adb/modules/), assigns a risk verdict — CLEAN / WARNING / DANGER —

and can keep watching installed modules for tampering. Everything runs on‑device; nothing

is uploaded unless you explicitly enable VirusTotal.

> ⚠️ Beta / compatibility notice. This is an early beta. It has been tested on APatch only.

> The design targets Magisk and KernelSU too (module layout, BusyBox paths, and env detection are

> handled), but those have not been verified on real devices yet. Treat verdicts as an *extra

> layer of defense*, not a guarantee.

---

Table of contents

  • [Features](#features)
  • [How it works](#how-it-works)
  • [Screens](#screens)
  • [Requirements](#requirements)
  • [Install](#install)
  • [Build from source](#build-from-source)
  • [Project structure](#project-structure)
  • [Detection rules](#detection-rules)
  • [Security & privacy notes](#security--privacy-notes)
  • [Support](#support)
  • [Contributing](#contributing)
  • [License](#license)
  • [Disclaimer](#disclaimer)

    • ---

    Features

  • **Device security score** — the Home tab shows an overall root‑security score (0–100) plus a

    • breakdown of dangerous / warning / ignored modules.

  • **Pre‑install scan** — pick a module `.zip`, get a verdict and a detailed, explainable list of

    • findings (file, line, snippet, plain‑language reason) before you flash it.

  • **Install gate** — CLEAN installs freely; WARNING asks for confirmation; DANGER is blocked

    • unless you override with fingerprint / device PIN (biometric prompt).

  • **Installed‑module scanning** — list modules in `/data/adb/modules/` and scan any of them on demand (root).
  • **Static payload de‑obfuscation** — hidden `base64` / `base64+gzip` / hex payloads are **decoded as

    • data (never executed)** and re‑scanned, so a concealed wget … | sh is revealed. The decoded

    plaintext is shown to you; an undecodable (encrypted) payload is flagged instead of hidden.

  • **Database‑driven verdicts** — "there's base64" is treated as a *weak* signal to avoid false

    • positives; a DANGER verdict is driven by the offline hash database, VirusTotal, or the actual

    decoded content.

  • **VirusTotal (optional, hash‑first)** — sends the SHA‑256 first; results are **cached for offline** use.

    • Public‑API rate limits (4/min, 500/day) are enforced automatically. Set the key in‑app; it's synced

    to the module via root.

  • **Offline antivirus database** — a local hash blocklist + regex signatures, extendable from any source

    • (see apatch-module/DATABASE.md).

  • **Realtime guard (root module)** — a lightweight `inotifyd` service (sleeps in the kernel, near‑zero

    • idle cost) that scans a module the moment it is installed or updated — no reboot, no full sweep of

    existing modules. Updating the ModGuard module itself re‑activates without a reboot too.

  • **Baseline & diff monitoring** — event‑driven (app open + boot + WorkManager), no polling daemon.

    • Volatile manager / magic‑mount files are excluded and non‑security changes don't alert, to avoid

    false positives on magic‑mount setups.

  • **Ignore list** — mark a module as safe so it stops notifying; keyed by **id + version**, so file

    • churn (e.g. magic mount) won't un‑ignore it, but a real update re‑arms the warning.

  • **Status / diagnostics tab** — permissions & access, all ModGuard services, and an on‑device crash log.
  • **English & Indonesian** — the UI follows your system language.
  • **CLI + recovery** — the same `:core` engine as a Termux‑runnable JAR, plus a pure‑shell scanner for

    • OrangeFox recovery.

    ---

    How it works

    Pre‑install scan & gate

    flowchart TD
    A[Pick module .zip] --> B[ZipModuleReader: parse module.prop,<br/>extract scripts, hash files]
    B --> C[Rule engine :core<br/>regex + heuristics]
    C --> D[PayloadDecoder<br/>decode base64/gzip/hex as DATA]
    D --> E[Re-scan decoded content]
    E --> F[ScoreCalculator: sum weights, clamp 0-100]
    F --> G{Verdict}
    G -->|CLEAN <30| H[Install allowed]
    G -->|WARNING 30-69| I[Confirm dialog]
    G -->|DANGER >=70| J[Blocked]
    J --> K[Override needs<br/>fingerprint / PIN]
    C -.optional.-> V[VirusTotal hash-first<br/>+ offline cache]
    V --> F
    I -->|proceed| H
    K -->|verified| H
    H --> L[Call APatch installer via su]

    Realtime guard (root module)

    flowchart LR
    S[install/update event] --> W[inotifyd watches modules<br/>+ modules_update staging]
    W -->|module installed/updated| X[debounce, compute fingerprint]
    X --> Y{in per-fingerprint cache?}
    Y -->|unchanged| Z[skip - no re-scan, no alert]
    Y -->|new / updated| Q[scan: static + offline DB + VirusTotal]
    Q --> R{DANGER and not ignored?}
    R -->|yes| N[log + am broadcast -> app notification]
    R -->|no| Z

    Purely event‑driven: it scans a module only when it is installed or updated (the staging dir is

    watched, so this needs no reboot), never sweeps already‑installed modules, and skips its own

    module. The app and module compute an identical canonical fingerprint (SHA‑256 over sorted

    relpath:filehash, excluding volatile manager / magic‑mount files), so caching and the ignore list

    work across both.

    ---

    Screens

    > 📸 Screenshots are not bundled yet (beta). Contributions welcome — drop PNGs in docs/screenshots/

    > and link them here. Navigation is a bottom bar with five tabs, plus two pushed screens:

    | Tab / screen | What it shows |

    |--------------|---------------|

    | Home | Device root‑security score (0–100) + dangerous / warning / ignored counts + guard status |

    | Scan | Pick a module .zip to scan before installing |

    | Installed | Modules under /data/adb/modules/, scan any on demand |

    | Warnings | Risky (not ignored) vs. ignored modules, with ignore / restore |

    | Status | Permissions & access, all ModGuard services, on‑device crash log |

    | *Scan result* (pushed) | Big verdict + score, module info, VirusTotal card, expandable findings (decoded payloads shown inline), install gate, "ignore" |

    | *Settings* (pushed) | Module service status, thresholds, offline AV database, monitoring, VirusTotal key, per‑rule toggles |

    ---

    Requirements

    | | |

    |---|---|

    | Device | Android 8.0+ (API 26) with root via APatch (tested), or Magisk / KernelSU (untested) |

    | App | The signed beta APK (see Install) |

    | Realtime module | BusyBox with inotifyd (bundled by APatch/Magisk/KSU) + toybox sha256sum |

    | VirusTotal (optional) | A free VirusTotal API key |

    | CLI (optional) | A JVM — on Termux: pkg install openjdk-17 |

    | Build | JDK 17, Android SDK (compileSdk 35), the bundled Gradle wrapper |

    ---

    Install

    App

    adb install dist/ModGuard-1.0.0-beta1.apk

    If you previously installed a debug build, uninstall it first (different signature). Beta‑to‑beta

    updates install over each other without uninstalling.

    Realtime guard module (optional)

    Flash dist/modguard-apatch.zip in APatch Manager → Modules → Install from storage. Reboot once

    to activate the watcher (or open the app's Status tab and tap *Restart* to activate without a

    reboot). After that, module installs/updates are scanned live, and updating ModGuard itself needs no

    reboot. Set the VirusTotal key from the app (Settings → VirusTotal → Save) — the app writes it to

    /data/adb/modguard/vt_api_key via root automatically.

    CLI (optional, Termux)

    pkg install openjdk-17
java -jar modguard-cli.jar <module.zip> [--db <hashes>] [--json]
# exit code: 0=CLEAN  1=WARNING  2=DANGER  3=error

    Recovery (OrangeFox)

    sh scripts/modguard-recovery.sh <module.zip>

    ---

    Build from source

    # Core unit tests (no device needed)
./gradlew :core:test

# Debug APK
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug        # app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk

# Signed beta release APK (needs keystore.properties, see below)
./gradlew :app:assembleRelease      # app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk

# Full verification (compiles debug+release, lint, tests)
./gradlew build

# CLI fat JAR
./gradlew :cli:fatJar               # cli/build/libs/modguard-cli.jar

# APatch module zip
sh scripts/build-apatch-module.sh   # dist/modguard-apatch.zip

    Signing (for release builds)

    Release signing reads a git‑ignored keystore.properties at the repo root:

    storeFile=modguard-beta.keystore
storePassword=your-store-password
keyAlias=modguard
keyPassword=your-key-password

    Generate a keystore once (kept out of version control; reuse it so updates stay installable):

    keytool -genkeypair -v -keystore modguard-beta.keystore -alias modguard \
  -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000

    Without keystore.properties, the release build is produced unsigned. minifyEnabled is

    off in beta on purpose (avoids R8 breaking reflection in kotlinx‑serialization / Compose).

    ---

    Project structure

    ModGuard/
├── app/                         # Android app (Kotlin + Jetpack Compose)
│   └── src/main/kotlin/dev/tomoeisozaki/modguard/
│       ├── MainActivity.kt · ModGuardApplication.kt
│       ├── auth/                # BiometricAuthenticator (DANGER override)
│       ├── data/                # Settings, secure key, AV DB, VT cache, ignore list stores
│       ├── diag/                # CrashLogger (uncaught-exception log for the Status tab)
│       ├── monitor/             # Baseline/diff, WorkManager, notifications, boot/alert receivers
│       ├── root/                # RootShell, installer, installed-module reader, ModuleBridge
│       ├── scan/                # ScannerFactory (wires settings + AV DB into the engine)
│       ├── vt/                  # VtRepository (cache + rate limit)
│       └── ui/                  # MainScaffold (bottom nav) + home, scan, installed, threats,
│                                #   status, result, settings, theme, components
├── core/                        # Pure-JVM engine (no Android deps) — shared with CLI & module logic
│   └── src/main/kotlin/dev/tomoeisozaki/modguard/core/
│       ├── model/               # ScanResult, Finding, Verdict, ModuleInfo, Signature, VtStats, …
│       ├── scanner/             # ZipModuleReader, ModulePropParser, PayloadDecoder, ModuleScanner
│       ├── rules/               # Rule engine, built-in rules, signature rules, scoring
│       └── vt/                  # VirusTotalClient (hash-first), RateLimiter
├── cli/                         # Kotlin JVM CLI (fat JAR) — same :core engine
├── apatch-module/               # Root module: module.prop, service.sh, boot-completed.sh,
│                                #   customize.sh, scan.sh (engine), DATABASE.md
├── scripts/                     # build-apatch-module.sh, modguard-recovery.sh, modguard-scan
├── samples/                     # Test module zips (clean / malicious / malformed)
├── dist/                        # Release artifacts (APK, module zip, CLI jar)
├── gradle/libs.versions.toml    # Version catalog
└── MODGUARD_PLANNING.md         # Original design brief

    Modules: :app (UI + root/Android glue) depends on :core; :cli depends on :core;

    :core is pure JVM and Android‑free so the exact same detection logic runs in the app, the CLI,

    and (re‑implemented in shell) the recovery script. The APatch module's scan.sh mirrors a subset

    of the rules in POSIX shell for on‑device root scanning without a JVM.

    ---

    Detection rules

    Rule‑based (no ML). Each finding carries a weight; the sum (clamped 0–100) maps to the verdict

    (<30 CLEAN, 30–69 WARNING, >=70 DANGER; thresholds are configurable). DANGER is driven mainly

    by the hash database / VirusTotal / decoded content, not by weak heuristics like "base64 present."

    | Rule | Detects | Weight |

    |------|---------|--------|

    | KNOWN_MALWARE_HASH | file/module hash in offline AV database | +80 |

    | VT_REPUTATION | VirusTotal detections (dynamic) / clean bonus | +30…+90 / −30 |

    | EXTERNAL_APK_INSTALL | pm install / download‑and‑install APK | +45 |

    | NET_FETCH_ON_BOOT | curl/wget in boot scripts | +40 |

    | *_DECODED | dangerous content found after decoding a hidden payload | rule's weight |

    | ENCRYPTED_PAYLOAD | hidden payload that can't be decoded to text (encrypted/binary) | +40 |

    | SENSITIVE_PATH_ACCESS | /data/data, keystore, other root tools' dirs | +30 |

    | NEW_SYSTEM_BINARY | new binary in system/bin|xbin|lib* | +25 |

    | CRON_PERSISTENCE | cron / init.d persistence | +25 |

    | SUSPICIOUS_SHELL | chmod 777, dd, remount rw /system | +20 |

    | OBFUSCATED_PAYLOAD | base64 -d / eval present (weak signal) | +15 |

    | PROP_INCOMPLETE | missing module.prop fields | +10 |

    | signatures | regex from the offline AV database | configurable |

    ---

    Security & privacy notes

  • **On‑device by default.** Static analysis is local. VirusTotal is opt‑in and hash‑first; the actual

    • module is only uploaded if you choose to.

  • **Payloads are never executed.** De‑obfuscation only *decodes* data (base64/gzip/hex). There is no

    • sandbox execution — decoding data is strictly safer.

  • **Secrets** (VirusTotal key) are stored with `EncryptedSharedPreferences`, never hard‑coded.
  • **VirusTotal Public API is free but not for commercial products.** Fine for personal / free community

    • use; commercial use requires a paid VirusTotal plan.

  • **Root responsibility.** The app requests `su` only to read `/data/adb/modules/` and to invoke the

    • existing APatch installer — it does not reimplement flashing.
